dissents.topic: How serious is the ClassName-only scope of the normalization

positions.position: P1 — the algorithm does not cover the stated invariant; a follow-up bug for #id\+ is almost guaranteed, but framed as 'correct for the reported bug'
P1 — complects the general concern (escape normalization is a value-level property of identifiers) with one incidental node type; same false negative still exists everywhere else
P1 — 'fixed one column of a multi-column bug', will earn three more bug reports next month; either widen or document and file the rest
P1 — partial LSP-violation across selector-node subtypes; either narrow the spec/rename to normalizeClassNameEscaping or extend implementation
P1 — algorithm fights a subset of the data shape; widen to every node kind that carries an escapable value
P1 — frame condition silently restricted with no argument; UNREASONED narrowing of the postcondition

dissents.topic: How to characterize the node.value = node.value self-assignment trick

positions.position: P2 — 'clever and correct' but warrants a stronger literate comment; pin parser version and document canonical form
P1 — complects intent with a language quirk; should be extracted into a pure normalizeEscaping(string) -> string helper, separating the value transform from the mutation
P2 — relies on undocumented side-effect; wrap with helper that asserts setter normalized, or pin a behavior test against postcss-selector-parser
P1 — SPEC-MISSING; depends on undocumented getter/setter behavior of a third-party type, requires JSDoc pre/postconditions and a direct unit test pinning the assumption
P2 — load-bearing cleverness future maintainers will read as a no-op and delete; wrap in named helper renormalizeEscaping(node)
P2 — smuggled side effect; eslint-disable is the tell, named helper required to make reasoning local instead of folkloric

dissents.topic: Status of the raws.value early-return guard

positions.position: P2 — load-bearing for correctness reasoning, not just perf; state as explicit invariant in the comment
P2 — incidental complexity for micro-optimization; would disappear if normalization were expressed as a pure string function
Mentioned as 'doing real work; good' but unmeasured — wants a benchmark note
P2 — LEAKY-ABSTRACTION; isolate behind typed helper hasRawValue(node)
P2 — type-unsafe optimization without a measurement; either measure and cite, or drop the gate
P2 — conflates absence-of-raws with absence-of-need-to-normalize; assumption is folklore, not invariant

issues.description: Normalization only handles ClassName; ID, attribute, type, and pseudo selectors with equivalent escapes still false-negative
issues.detail: The bug class — CSS escape equivalence — applies to every identifier the selector grammar accepts (#u-m\+ vs #u-m\00002b, [data-x=\+], escaped tag names, pseudo-class arguments), but the patch gates renormalization on parser.isClassName(node). All six reviewers independently flagged this as the central scope problem: the implementation honors the contract for one node subtype only. Either widen to every node kind that exposes a value getter/setter with the same canonicalization behavior, or narrow the function's name and JSDoc to honestly state the scope and file follow-ups for the other identifier kinds.

issues.description: Correctness depends on an undocumented postcss-selector-parser getter/setter side effect, with no spec or pinning test
issues.detail: node.value = node.value works only because the ClassName setter re-encodes through the escape routine — an internal behavior of a third-party library cited via a permalink rather than an API contract. If postcss-selector-parser ever changes ClassName to a plain field (perf cleanup, refactor, or a new Node subtype overriding value), this rule silently regresses to the pre-fix bug with no test signal. Liskov and Dijkstra escalate this to P1; Torvalds and Knuth ask for a behavior test pinning the parser-setter assumption and a recorded parser version; Hickey and Pike want it extracted into a named helper (renormalizeEscaping / normalizeEscaping) so intent is local and the dependence is documented.

issues.description: node.value = node.value complects intent with a library quirk; the operation reads as a no-op without the comment
issues.detail: Hickey argues the operation is easy (short) but not simple: the intent is a value transformation on a string (unescape then canonical re-escape) and pulling it into a pure normalizeEscaping(string) -> string helper would separate the value transform from the mutation, make it testable in isolation, and stop depending on a third-party setter that may change. Dijkstra calls the self-assignment a smuggled side effect, with the eslint-disable as the tell.

issues.description: Test coverage proves two members of the escape equivalence class but not the class
issues.detail: The added reject cases (\00002b vs \+, \2b vs \00002b) all exercise .u-m\xx class selectors. Reviewers want broader coverage to prove the equivalence claim: uppercase vs lowercase hex (\2B vs \2b), space-terminated hex (\2b vs \2b), non-ASCII codepoints, surrogate pairs, escapes at start of identifier, escapes of digits otherwise illegal as first char, plus a negative test confirming .u-m\+ and .u-n\+ remain distinct. Tests should also pin the scope of the fix — either passing cases for ID/attribute/tag/pseudo or accept cases that document known gaps.

issues.description: Tests exercise the rule end-to-end, never the normalizeNodeEscaping helper directly
issues.detail: Dijkstra notes that the unit under repair is the helper, yet every new test goes through no-duplicate-selectors. A regression in normalizeNodeEscaping that does not affect this rule, or that affects another consumer of normalizeSelector, will not be caught. Recommends direct unit tests on the helper's interface over a representative set of escape forms.

issues.description: node.value = node.value relies on an undocumented postcss-selector-parser side effect and warrants a stronger literate comment
issues.detail: Knuth wants the comment to record the canonical form chosen by the setter (character-escape vs hex), why the raws.value guard is a performance optimization rather than a correctness requirement, and the postcss-selector-parser version this was verified against, to protect against silent upstream regressions.

issues.description: raws.value guard couples correctness to an internal field and conflates absence-of-raws with absence-of-need-to-normalize
issues.detail: The early return if (!node.raws?.value) return; is labeled as a perf shortcut but is load-bearing for correctness: the claim is that when raws.value is absent, node.value is already canonical. Multiple reviewers flag the same concern with different emphases: Knuth wants the invariant stated explicitly; Hickey notes the optimization disappears if normalization is a pure string function; Liskov calls it a leaky abstraction reaching past the public type and wants a typed helper hasRawValue(node); Pike calls it a speed hack without a measurement (either justify with a number or drop the gate); Dijkstra notes the assumption is parser folklore and would silently reintroduce the bug if a future parser populates value without raws.value. All want either a test that pins the invariant or removal of the gate.

issues.description: @ts-expect-error plus eslint-disable in five lines signals an under-articulated abstraction
issues.detail: Two suppressions in a tiny function: @ts-expect-error masks a real type gap on raws.value (could be addressed by augmenting the type locally or using a typed accessor), and the no-self-assign disable buries the intent. Torvalds reads it as 'we got it working, move on' for a util that runs on every selector in every lint; Liskov frames it as a leaky abstraction; Dijkstra and Pike both call for a named helper whose body performs the assignment with documented pre/postconditions.

issues.description: Performance is unmeasured for a hot path
issues.detail: normalizeSelector runs per rule per pass. Adding parser.isClassName plus a node.raws?.value access per walked node is cheap but unverified on large real stylesheets. Torvalds wants a one-line benchmark note in the PR or commit message; Knuth notes complexity is unchanged asymptotically and is fine but should be named honestly; Pike argues the perf gate itself needs a measurement or should be dropped.

issues.description: Two passes of work per node where one would do; ordering invariant is implicit
issues.detail: Pike: normalizeSelector now does an up-front normalizeNodeEscaping on the root plus another in-walk pass for whitespace/comments; the cleaner shape is a single normalize applied uniformly to root and descendants. Liskov: the ordering of escape -> whitespace/comments -> node order matters, but the contract is not stated; a one-line invariant comment at the top of normalizeSelector would make the module's promise legible.

synthesis.summary: All six reviewers converged independently on the same central P1: the fix works for the reported class-selector case but gates renormalization on parser.isClassName, while CSS escape equivalence is a property of every identifier the selector grammar accepts (IDs, attributes, tag names, pseudo arguments) — so the same false-negative bug class remains open elsewhere. Five of six also flagged that correctness rests on an undocumented postcss-selector-parser getter/setter side effect, cited only via a permalink, with no behavior test pinning the assumption; Liskov and Dijkstra escalate this to P1 (SPEC-MISSING / TESTED-NOT-PROVED), while Knuth, Torvalds, and Pike treat it as P2 needing literate documentation and a parser-version pin. The strongest preserved disagreement is about the node.value = node.value mechanism itself: Hickey and Dijkstra want it extracted into a pure named helper because the self-assignment complects intent with a library quirk (and the eslint-disable is the tell), whereas Knuth, Torvalds, and Pike call it clever-but-correct and accept it with stronger comments or a wrapping helper for readability. Secondary P2 consensus: tests prove two members of the escape equivalence class rather than the class (hex case, whitespace-terminated escapes, non-ASCII, negative tests, and direct unit tests on the helper are all requested), the raws.value early-return couples correctness to an internal field and is unmeasured, and the two-walk structure plus implicit ordering invariant could be tightened.
